solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Rush nurse injecting drug (6)

indicatorNotes.injecting: the nurse injects the drug, so E goes inside CARER

annotation.surface: A hurried nurse jabbing a patient with some medicine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rush' is a verb here: to career is to hurtle along. 'Drug' is almost always E for ecstasy in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: To career is to rush headlong, as a runaway car careers down a hill.

entries.clue: Start brief remark on church (8)

indicatorNotes.brief: a brief word is cut short, losing its last letter
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: COMMENT with its last letter cut off

annotation.surface: Someone opening proceedings with a quick word about the church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like an instruction to take a first letter, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the formal Latin-derived verb for begin or start, as in 'let the games begin'.

entries.clue: Extremely rare permit covering vehicle is pertinent (8)

indicatorNotes.Extremely: take only the extremes, the first and last letters, of 'rare'
indicatorNotes.covering: LET covers VAN, holding it inside

annotation.surface: A remark that a licence to drive some vehicle is seldom relevant.
annotation.walkthrough: RE followed by LE(VAN)T.
annotation.definitionFit: Relevant and pertinent both mean bearing on the matter in hand.

entries.clue: Thus monster heads north (4)

indicatorNotes.heads north: in a down clue, going north means reading from the bottom up

annotation.surface: A monster lumbering off northwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heads north' only works as a reversal because this is a down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin word borrowed into English logic, meaning therefore: 'I think, thus I am'.

entries.clue: Pressure hotel workers to drink some unrestricted spirits (8)

indicatorNotes.to drink: the workers swallow the next piece, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.some unrestricted: 'some' without its restricting outer letters leaves its middle, OM

blocks.note: H = hotel in the phonetic alphabet
worker ants: ants are the crossword's standard workers
SOME with its outer letters removed

annotation.surface: Pushing hotel staff to down some liquor with no limits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' sits beside 'drink', so it reads as alcohol; it means ghosts. Worker ants are the crossword's standard workers.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the ghostly sense of spirits: apparitions of the dead, not bottles of gin.

entries.clue: I forgot he had developed hangover cure (4,2,3,3)

indicatorNotes.developed: the letters are worked into a new form

annotation.surface: Someone who has forgotten that a friend came down with a hangover.
annotation.walkthrough: The hair of the dog is a morning drink taken to ease a hangover, from the old idea of treating a dog bite with the dog's hair.
annotation.definitionFit: The hair of the dog is the proverbial remedy for a hangover: more of what caused it.

entries.clue: North American setter’s handle (4)

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as ME

annotation.surface: A remark about an American dog's name, or the handle on an American's setting tool.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is': NA plus ME is a handle. 'Setter' suggests a dog breed; it is the person who wrote the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name, as in a CB radio or online handle.

entries.clue: One kid unexpectedly made a sound like a pig (6)

annotation.definition: made a sound like a pig

indicatorNotes.unexpectedly: the letters turn up in an unexpected order

annotation.surface: A child suddenly snorting like a pig.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly the answer: a kid oinking.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is a descriptive paraphrase of the verb: the grunting noise pigs make, past tense.

entries.clue: Discontented spy sat exam for organisation (6)

indicatorNotes.Discontented: dis-content-ed: each word loses its contents, its middle

annotation.surface: An unhappy spy sitting a recruitment test for an agency.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discontented' reads as unhappy, but splits as dis-contented: emptied of contents. It applies to all three words after it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an organisation in the sense of an orderly arrangement or method, not a company.

entries.clue: Animal ignored, somewhat evil (6)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: only some of the words are used

annotation.surface: A creature left alone and turning a bit nasty.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the word break: the end of 'Animal' and the start of 'ignored'.
annotation.definitionFit: Malign as an adjective means evil or harmful.

entries.clue: Add-ons I’m getting tailored for suit (8)

indicatorNotes.getting tailored: tailoring cuts and rearranges the material

annotation.surface: Someone having extras added to a suit by a tailor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tailored' and 'suit' paint clothing, but the suit is one of the four in a pack of cards.
annotation.definitionFit: Diamonds are one of the four suits in a pack of cards.

entries.clue: Pay airmen our ten bucks (12)

indicatorNotes.bucks: bucking like a horse throws the letters about

annotation.surface: An instruction to pay ten dollars to each of the pilots.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bucks' looks like dollars going with 'Pay'; it is a verb telling the letters to leap about.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the formal word for the pay or salary someone receives for work.

entries.clue: English sailors avoiding adult sin (4)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: the sailors avoid A, which is left out

blocks.note: the navy is a body of sailors
A = adult, as in film ratings; removed from NAVY

annotation.surface: English seamen steering clear of grown-up vice.
annotation.walkthrough: E + N(A)VY with the A taken out.
annotation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins.

entries.clue: Sit back, following ace fabulist (5)

indicatorNotes.back: the word for 'sit' is read backwards
indicatorNotes.following: the reversed piece comes after the ace

blocks.note: A = ace, as on a playing card
to sit for a portrait is to pose

annotation.surface: Someone told to lean back behind a champion storyteller.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue gives POSE reversed before the ace, but 'following' puts it after.
annotation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek writer of fables.

entries.clue: Present in that place wants opening (4)

indicatorNotes.wants opening: to want is to lack, so the phrase lacks its opening, the first letter

blocks.note: there = in that place; drop the T

annotation.surface: Someone at the scene who is looking for a way in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present' is an adjective here, as in answering a register: here.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective sense of present, in attendance: what a pupil answers at roll call.

entries.clue: Tolerate criticism (5)

blocks.note: put up with, informal British: 'I can't bear him'
harsh comments, informal British: fans 'give' a player this

annotation.surface: Advice to put up with being criticised.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses are informal British: 'I can't stick him' and 'the fans gave him stick'.
annotation.definitionFit: Stick means both to tolerate and harsh criticism.

entries.clue: Complete baby awful on vacation (5)

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
AWFUL emptied, leaving A and L

annotation.surface: A toddler behaving dreadfully on a family holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' paints a holiday; it means vacated, emptied.
annotation.definitionFit: Complete and total both mean utter, as in a total disaster.

entries.clue: Reasons not to time noisy argument in building (12)

blocks.note: the pros and cons: cons are reasons against
a ruction is a noisy row

annotation.surface: Arguments against timing a loud row inside a building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not to time' seems to belong together, but 'Reasons not to' is the unit: CONS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anything built is a structure, and the act of building is also meant.

entries.clue: Clergyman providing support for policeman and film-maker (8)

indicatorNotes.providing support for: in a down clue, the rector stands below the policeman, holding him up

blocks.note: a rector is a parish priest

annotation.surface: A vicar backing up a police officer and a filmmaker.
annotation.walkthrough: The clergyman comes first in the clue but last in the answer: supporting means going underneath in a down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by role: the person in charge of shooting a movie is the one credited as its maker.

entries.clue: One might not believe part of explicit song appropriate, on reflection (8)

indicatorNotes.part of: the answer is only part of the words that follow
indicatorNotes.on reflection: reflected, as in a mirror, it reads backwards

annotation.surface: Someone wondering whether a crude song is fitting, after thinking it over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' reads as 'after thinking', but it asks for a mirror image.
annotation.definitionFit: An agnostic neither believes nor disbelieves in God, so might not believe.

entries.clue: Speeding up triage, cancel shifts (12)

annotation.surface: A hospital hurrying the sorting of patients by scrapping staff shifts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shifts' looks like hospital work rotas; it is a verb, rearranging the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: gaining speed, as a car does when the pedal goes down.

entries.clue: Seafood side in southern India (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the side goes inside S and I

blocks.note: a side or faction, as in the two camps
I = India in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A seafood side dish served in the south of India.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Side' looks like a side dish; it is a camp, a faction. S(CAMP)I.
annotation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines, usually served breaded and fried.

entries.clue: Overly enthusiastic with weapon, initially getting hauled outside (4-2)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the initial letter of each of the following words

blocks.note: first letters of Getting Hauled Outside

annotation.surface: A trigger-happy gunman getting dragged out of the room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hauled outside' looks like one phrase for ejection, but 'initially' covers all three words.
annotation.definitionFit: Gung-ho means overly eager, especially about fighting.

entries.clue: Youngster holding large bat (4)

blocks.note: a cub is a young animal, or a Cub Scout
L = large, as on clothing sizes

annotation.surface: A child gripping an oversized bat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bat' suggests the animal beside 'Youngster'; it is the thing you hit with.
annotation.definitionFit: A club and a bat are both things for hitting a ball.

entries.clue: Expressions of thanks and contempt forbidden (5)

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks

annotation.surface: Saying thank you and jeering both being banned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Expressions of' governs both halves: thanks gives TA, contempt gives BOO.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a Tongan-derived word for things banned by custom or social rule.

entries.clue: Periodically dreams of protest (4)

indicatorNotes.Periodically: at regular intervals: every other letter

blocks.note: D r E a M s O f

annotation.surface: Someone who now and then dreams of joining a protest.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters come from across both words, 'dreams' and 'of'.
annotation.definitionFit: A demo is short for a demonstration, a protest march.

entries.clue: First couples from Mexico should work well together (4)

indicatorNotes.First couples from: take the first two letters of each word

blocks.note: the first letter pair of MExico
the first letter pair of SHould

annotation.surface: A claim that the first married pairs from Mexico get on well.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First couples' sounds like newlyweds; it means the first pair of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Things mesh when they fit together smoothly, like gears.

entries.clue: Article on upper-class artist’s distinctive quality (4)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the article sits on top of the rest

blocks.note: U = upper-class, as in U and non-U

annotation.surface: A piece about the special something a posh painter has.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s means 'is': A + U + RA is a distinctive quality.
annotation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or quality surrounding someone.

entries.clue: Drawing in publication with new quote going round (8)

indicatorNotes.going round: the quote turns round and reads backwards

annotation.surface: An illustration in a magazine next to a fresh quotation doing the rounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawing in publication' reads as a picture in a magazine; 'Drawing in' is the definition, meaning attracting.
annotation.definitionFit: Something magnetic draws things in, attracting them.

entries.clue: I disapprove of leaders of trade unions talking repeatedly (3-3)

indicatorNotes.leaders of: the leading letters of the words
indicatorNotes.repeatedly: something done repeatedly happens again, so the three letters appear a second time

blocks.note: first letters of Trade Unions Talking

annotation.surface: Someone objecting to union bosses who never stop talking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I disapprove' is the definition: tut-tut is what you say to express it.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is what the exclamation says: the clicking noise people make to show disapproval.

entries.clue: Rigorous control of press pass (4,4)

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them
to hand something over is to pass it

annotation.surface: Strict government control over the newspapers and their passes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Press' reads as the newspapers, but it is the verb, as with clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: Ruling with an iron hand means exercising strict, rigorous control.

entries.clue: Material from brilliant Republican in charge (6)

annotation.surface: Evidence gathered from a clever Republican running things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like evidence or information here; it is cloth.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: woven cloth, the material clothes are made from.
